claim: A PLOS Genetics Crohn disease study mapped a 5p13.1 susceptibility region to a gene desert and reported modulation of PTGER4 expression as a plausible mechanism for the Crohn signal.
future_grounding_route: Use only as Crohn-side functional context unless exact variants and expression/QTL effects are imported and harmonized against the project's PTGER4 MS/IBD direction framework.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: PTGER4 mixed shared/distinct signal closes naive transfer

project_use: External Crohn-side PTGER4 functional-direction context supporting why PTGER4 transfer requires signal-specific direction rather than generic target overlap.
relationship_note: This supports Crohn-side PTGER4 regulatory biology but does not validate a direction-matched MS intervention.

source.citation: Libioulle et al. Novel Crohn disease locus identified by genome-wide association maps to a gene desert on 5p13.1 and modulates expression of PTGER4. PLOS Genetics. 2007.
source.label: PLOS Genetics PTGER4 Crohn expression-modulation study

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: PubMed bibliographic metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: V50 stores bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrased claim only; do not redistribute article text or treat it as project-grounded evidence.

why_unverifiable: The project has not rerun the external Crohn GWAS/expression analysis or harmonized it to MS direction in the external layer.
